title: Shubi language
extract: Shubi is a Bantu language spoken by the Shubi people in north-western Tanzania. It may use labiodental plosives, as phonemes, rather than as allophones of. Peter Ladefoged wrote:We have heard labiodental stops made by a Shubi speaker whose teeth were sufficiently close together to allow him to make an airtight labiodental closure. For this speaker this sound was clearly in contrast with a bilabial stop; but we suspect that the majority of Shubi speakers make the contrast one of bilabial stop versus labial-labiodental affricate, rather than bilabial versus labiodental stop.
